title: Consistency & Context Engine — Cross-Chapter Consistency + Context-Aware Suggestions
description: Enhance cross-chapter consistency checking with character name conflict detection, timeline verification, unresolved plot thread tracking, and trait drift detection. Create context-aware suggestion engine that assembles relevant story bible entries, memory, and character profiles based on current writing content. Register MCP endpoints /consistency/cross-chapter, /suggestions/context-aware.
action: Create src-ts/src/agents/consistency-engine.ts with CrossChapterConsistencyChecker class. Create src-ts/src/agents/context-assembler.ts with ContextAwareAssembler class. Create src-ts/src/mcp/endpoints/consistency-engine.ts with POST /consistency/cross-chapter and POST /suggestions/context-aware endpoints. ConsistencyChecker takes chapter array and detects name conflicts, timeline issues, unresolved threads, trait drift. ContextAssembler takes current text + workspace and returns assembled context from story bible + memory + character profiles.

convergence.verification: Call CrossChapterConsistencyChecker with multi-chapter test data containing intentional conflicts, verify all conflict types detected. Call ContextAssembler with text referencing known characters/locations, verify relevant context is assembled.
convergence.definition_of_done: Cross-chapter consistency checker detects name conflicts, timeline issues, unresolved threads, and trait drift across chapters. Context assembler retrieves relevant story bible/memory/character data based on current text content.

files.change: New file: CrossChapterConsistencyChecker class with check(chapters) returning ConsistencyReport with nameConflicts[], timelineIssues[], unresolvedThreads[], traitDrifts[]
Unit tests: detect name conflicts across chapters, detect timeline contradictions, detect unresolved plot threads
New file: ContextAwareAssembler class with assembleContext(text, workspace) returning assembled context string from story bible + memory + character profiles
Unit tests: context assembly with known characters, story bible integration, memory retrieval
POST /consistency/cross-chapter (accepts chapters[], returns ConsistencyReport), POST /suggestions/context-aware (accepts text + workspace, returns assembled context)

implementation: Define ConsistencyReport interface: { overallScore: number; nameConflicts: Array<{character, chapter1, chapter2, description}>; timelineIssues: Array<{event1, event2, description}>; unresolvedThreads: Array<{thread, lastMentioned, description}>; traitDrifts: Array<{character, trait, chapter1, chapter2, description}> }
detectNameConflicts: Extract character names from each chapter, find inconsistent references (e.g., 'John' vs 'Jon', character appearing with different roles)
detectTimelineIssues: Use LLM to verify temporal ordering of events across chapters
detectUnresolvedThreads: Track plot elements introduced but never resolved in subsequent chapters
detectTraitDrifts: Compare character descriptions/behaviors across chapters for inconsistencies

Implement ContextAwareAssembler.assembleContext(currentText: string, workspace: ProjectWorkspaceContext): string — extract entity mentions from current text, query story bible for matching entries, query memory for relevant context, query character profiles, assemble into structured context string
Create MCP endpoints following existing pattern from chat.ts
Write tests with multi-chapter test data containing intentional consistency issues

unit: context-assembler.test.ts: context assembly with entity mentions

reference.pattern: Existing runConsistencyCheck in desktop/src/api/client.ts — extend the pattern for cross-chapter analysis
reference.examples: runWorkspaceConsistencyCheck shows the UI integration pattern

rationale.chosen_approach: Combine consistency checking and context assembly into one task because they share the same workspace context model and both need to query story bible + character data. Separating would create unnecessary duplication.
decision_factors: Existing consistency check already works for single chapters
Context assembly is needed for both consistency and suggestions
rationale.tradeoffs: Combined task is larger but avoids duplicating workspace context resolution logic

risks: Cross-chapter analysis with LLM may be slow for large manuscripts — mitigate with chapter-level parallelism
Entity extraction accuracy depends on text quality — start with LLM-based extraction, refine later
